commitResults.messageTitle: Cap phone and email length before validation
commitResults.messageBody:
A phone of about 5000 digits was accepted by add, but the next launch
crashed with a StackOverflowError while loading the data file, and no
.bak copy was made. The phone regex recursed once per digit, and data
loading runs on a thread with a smaller stack than the UI thread. Long
emails had the same problem through the local-part regex.

Phone numbers are now capped at 30 characters and emails at 254, the
practical limit for an email address. The length is checked before
any regex runs, so an over-long value from a command or from the data
file gets the normal constraint message, and loading falls back to
the .bak path instead of crashing.

The phone regex is also rewritten to use a lookahead plus a character
class, which accepts the same inputs but matches in a loop, so it
cannot overflow even without the length cap.
Avoid duplicate tags that differ only by case

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject a blank follow-up date on add
commitResults.messageBody:
Typing f/ with nothing after it on add showed the DD-MM-YYYY format
error, which suggests the date was written wrongly. On edit the same
input clears the follow-up, so users may expect it to mean "no
follow-up" on add too.

Check for a blank value first and tell the user to leave out f/
instead. Edit keeps its current behaviour, where a blank f/ clears the
date.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept due days with any number of leading zeros
commitResults.messageBody:
The days argument was limited to 9 characters so Integer.parseInt
could not overflow. That also rejected values such as 0000000365,
which are in range, while 000000365 was accepted.

Strip leading zeros first and limit the remaining digits to the length
of MAX_DAYS. Overflow is still impossible, and the result no longer
depends on how many zeros were typed.

commitResults.messageTitle: End the due days error with a full stop
commitResults.messageBody:
The other parser errors end with a full stop, but the invalid days
message for due did not. Add it, and update the DG manual test that
quotes the message so testers see the exact text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sort due ties by name with a collator
commitResults.messageBody:
Contacts due on the same date were ordered with CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER,
which compares UTF-16 values, so a name such as Émile Tan came after
Zack Lim. Names may start with accented letters, so this looked wrong.

Use a Collator for Locale.ROOT, which puts accented letters next to
their base letter and does not depend on the user's locale.

commitResults.messageTitle: Format due counts with the root locale
commitResults.messageBody:
String.format uses the default locale, so on a machine set to a locale
such as ar-EG the due count was printed in Arabic-Indic digits and the
due tests failed. The app's messages are English, so the count should
always use ASCII digits.

Pass Locale.ROOT to both due messages and add a test that runs the
command under ar-EG.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test DueCommand equality with another day's clock
commitResults.messageBody:
DueCommand.equals compares the clock as well as the number of days,
but no test used a different clock, so dropping the clock check went
unnoticed. hashCode and toString were never run either.

Add an equals case with a clock one day later, and cover hashCode and
toString.

commitResults.messageTitle: Pin the time zone used by parsed due commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The parser tests compared two commands built with the default clock,
so they would still pass if DueCommand switched to a UTC clock. For
users in Singapore that would make due a day behind each morning.

Build the expected commands with Clock.systemDefaultZone() explicitly,
and add a test that sets the default zone to Pacific/Kiritimati and
checks the parsed command uses it and not UTC. The test does not
depend on the zone the tests run in.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the missing fields when add is incomplete
commitResults.messageBody:
An add command without one of n/, p/, e/ or a/ showed only the
generic usage text, so the user had to work out which field was
left out. The use case says the app should explain which details
need correction.

Report the missing prefixes first, in the order of the command
format, followed by the usage on the next line. Text before the
first prefix still shows the usage alone, since it is unclear which
field it was meant for.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify tag rules and accept accented letters
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags used the ASCII-only \p{Alnum} pattern, so t/café was rejected
even though names accept accented letters, and every tag error showed
the terse "Tag names should be alphanumeric" with no full stop.

Tags are still a single word of letters and digits, but letters and
digits now mean any Unicode letter or digit, matching names. Input is
normalised to NFC first, so a decomposed accent is the same tag as the
composed one.

Tag equality now compares the lower-cased name (Locale.ROOT) in both
equals and hashCode, so they agree for non-ASCII case pairs such as
the Turkish dotted and dotless i. The list t/ filter uses the same
rule.

The constraint message now states the rule with an example, and the
user guide add section lists what a tag may contain.

commitResults.messageTitle: Pin the data file's JSON key names in tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The storage tests only save and load through the same adapter classes,
so renaming a key such as status, followUp or interactionNotes in
JsonAdaptedPerson kept every test green while users' saved data was
silently dropped on the next launch.

Add a hand-written fixture in the exact on-disk format, with one
contact that uses every field and one older contact without status,
followUp or interactionNotes. DataFileFormatTest loads it through
JsonAddressBookStorage and compares it with PersonBuilder contacts,
checks that the older contact falls back to PROSPECT with no follow-up
and no notes, and saves a known contact to check the written key names
with the Jackson tree model.

The key check only requires the expected keys to be present, so adding
a new field does not break it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject unusable GUI settings in preferences file
commitResults.messageBody:
A preferences.json with "guiSettings": null made the app crash on
launch. Jackson writes the null straight into UserPrefs, so no
DataLoadingException was raised, and initPrefs saved the null back.
Every later launch crashed until the user deleted the file by hand.

Window coordinates near the int limits also abort the app on macOS
inside the native window code, and null, zero, negative or non-finite
sizes give a broken window that is then saved again.

Let's check the GUI settings after reading the file and throw a
DataLoadingException when they are unusable. MainApp already handles
that exception by logging a warning, using the default preferences and
overwriting the bad file, so the app starts and recovers on its own.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make tag case matching consistent for Unicode
commitResults.messageBody:
Comparing lowercased names misses some case pairs that Unicode
letters bring in. The Greek capital sigma has two lowercase forms, so
"ΟΣ" and "οσ" were different tags. Lowercasing an NFC string can also
give a string that is not NFC, so U+03AA U+0301 did not equal its own
lowercase form and list t/ with that exact tag name missed it.

Build the comparison key by lowercasing, then uppercasing, with NFC
normalisation after each step. Variants that share an uppercase form
are now one tag, and equals, hashCode and the list filter all use the
same key. As a side effect "straße" and "STRASSE" are one tag, and the
dotless i matches I, as String.equalsIgnoreCase already did.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject emoji built from marks in tags
commitResults.messageBody:
A digit followed by U+FE0F and U+20E3 is the keycap emoji, but it
passed the tag check because any combining mark was allowed after the
first character. A trailing variation selector could also make an
invisible difference between two tags that look the same.

Allow only non-spacing and spacing combining marks, and leave out the
variation selectors, so vowel signs in Hindi, Tamil and Thai still
work. Add TagTest cases for zero-width characters, emoji, digits from
other scripts, Tamil, a 1000 character tag and a prefix-like tag.
Add integration tests for command sequences

commitResults.messageTitle: Check the fraction of a second in saved notes
commitResults.messageBody:
The save test only checked a note timestamp with no fraction, so
saving timestamps rounded down to whole seconds went unnoticed. Also
use Status.DEFAULT instead of a hard-coded status name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cap window size read from the preferences file
commitResults.messageBody:
A huge window height with an ordinary y position still pushed the
native window frame past the int range and aborted the app on every
launch. Reject sizes above 1,000,000 like the coordinates. Also let
the throw helpers use assertThrows and name the boundary test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cap tag length and tighten tag characters
commitResults.messageBody:
Case mapping a long tag was very slow, because lowercasing a run of
Greek sigma gets slower the longer the run is. The case-insensitive
key was also worked out again on every equals and hashCode call, so a
single 100k character tag could stall add, list t/ and startup for
minutes.

Tags are now capped at 50 characters, counted after composing
accents, and the length is checked before any other work. The key is
worked out once when the tag is made, and the list filter compares
these keys, so t/STRASSE and t/straße also give equal filters. Plain
ASCII tags skip normalization and the pattern, which keeps loading a
large data file as fast as before.

Tags also accepted characters that draw nothing, such as the Hangul
fillers, the combining grapheme joiner and the Mongolian variation
selectors, plus unlimited stacks of combining marks. These are now
rejected, with at most two marks on each letter. Digits must be
decimal digits, so number symbols such as one half, superscript two
and circled one are rejected.

An old data file with a tag over 50 characters fails to load, so it
is copied to the usual .bak file and the app starts empty, like any
other invalid data file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Look up the list tag filter in the tag set
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags now keep their case-insensitive key and use it for both equals
and hashCode, so a contact's tag set can answer the list t/ filter
with one lookup instead of checking every tag in turn. With 200 tags
per contact this makes the filter about ten times faster.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove an unused tag comparison helper
commitResults.messageBody:
Only the tests called it. equals and hashCode already use the same
cached key, and the tests now check equality directly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that sort order affects model equality
commitResults.messageBody:
ModelManager.equals compares the displayed list, so two models with the
same contacts but a different active sort order should not be equal.
Command tests rely on this when they compare against an expected model,
yet nothing failed if equals ignored the order.

Add a test that sorts one model in reverse name order, checks that it
is not equal to an unsorted copy, then resets the filter and checks
that the two are equal again.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix data transfer steps in the UG FAQ
commitResults.messageBody:
The FAQ told users to overwrite the data file the app creates on the
new computer. A fresh install does not create data/addressbook.json
until a command changes contact data, so there was nothing to
overwrite. Read-only commands such as list do not create it either.

Tell users to create the data folder themselves and copy their old
addressbook.json into it while the app is closed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct when the DG says the data file is recreated
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands that do not change contact data no longer save, so list does
not recreate a deleted data file. Name commands that do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject trailing content in JSON data files
commitResults.messageBody:
JsonUtil read data files with ObjectMapper#readValue, which stops after
the first JSON value. A data file with a second address book, a stray
brace or other text after the closing brace loaded only the first part
without any error. No backup was made, and the next save overwrote the
file, so the extra contacts were lost.

Read the value through a JsonParser and require that only whitespace
follows it. Anything else now fails with an IOException that gives the
line and column of the extra content, so readJsonFile throws
DataLoadingException and the usual backup and empty start path runs.
This covers both the address book and the preferences file.

Jackson 2.7 has no FAIL_ON_TRAILING_TOKENS, so the check is done by
hand instead of upgrading Jackson.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention trailing text in data file guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Extra text after the final closing brace of the data file now makes the
file invalid. Say so in the sentence that explains the backup, so users
who paste contacts after the brace know why the app started empty.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add planned enhancements appendix to DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG has no Planned Enhancements appendix yet. Known flaws that we
will not fix before the feature freeze can still be reported as bugs
in the PE.

Add the appendix after the manual testing appendix. It states the team
size and lists 10 enhancements, the maximum for a team of 5. Each item
gives the current behaviour with the exact message, and the planned
change with sample input and output.

The items cover the data file being overwritten by a second window or
a hand edit, prefix parsing (capitalised prefixes, a/l and a/p in
names, tabs), index checks (missing space, very large numbers,
non-ASCII digits), and the clear, find and edit messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note the two-copies limitation in UG known issues
commitResults.messageBody:
The planned enhancement for overwritten saves needs a matching UG

commitResults.messageTitle: Log that a missing data file is not created yet
commitResults.messageBody:
Startup said it was creating a new data file, but the file is only

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix three planned enhancements and a UG note
commitResults.messageBody:
Make the overwrite item one change (a content hash refreshed after

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy the trailing content comment and UG wording
commitResults.messageBody:
The token location is not always exact, and spaces or blank lines
after the final brace are still allowed.
Document name abbreviations and address prefix behavior

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix date-dependent due docs and diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG manual test for due used fixed October 2026 dates, so the
expected results only held on one day. Use a past date, today's date
and a date 3 days from today instead, and phrase the expected result
messages relative to those dates.

Add a UG note that a contact leaves the due list after done, since it
no longer has a follow-up, and that list shows it again.

The due sequence diagram showed parse("7"), but CommandInputParser
passes the arguments with their leading space. Show parse(" 7").
Clarify edit feedback for tags and follow-ups

commitResults.messageTitle: Save edits that only change tag letter case
commitResults.messageBody:
Editing a tag's letter case, e.g. "edit 1 t/vip" on a contact tagged
VIP, showed the new spelling but never wrote it to the data file, so
the old spelling came back after a restart.

LogicManager#execute skips saving when the contact list is unchanged,
using AddressBook#equals. Tags compare case-insensitively so that VIP
and vip are one tag, which makes such an edit look like no change.

Add AddressBook#isIdenticalTo, which also compares the exact tag
spellings that the data file stores, and change the one comparison
line in LogicManager#execute to use it, to fix the interaction between
the save check and case-insensitive tags. Tag equality is unchanged.
Every other contact field already compares the exact value it saves.

Contacts that a command does not touch are the same objects in both
lists, so the extra check is skipped for them and read-only commands
cost the same as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject data files that are not valid UTF-8
commitResults.messageBody:
FileUtil#readFromFile decoded files with new String(bytes, UTF-8),
which silently replaces malformed bytes with U+FFFD. A data file with
a stray byte such as 0xFF in an address loaded without any error, no
.bak was made, and the next save wrote U+FFFD over the original text
for good. This is not what the user guide promises for invalid files.

Decode with a CharsetDecoder that reports malformed input instead.
The resulting IOException names the file and the byte offset, and
JsonUtil#readJsonFile turns it into a DataLoadingException, so the
existing path runs: the data file is copied to addressbook.json.bak
and the app starts empty. Preferences go through the same method, so
an invalid preferences file now falls back to the defaults.

Valid UTF-8, including emoji, CJK, Tamil and combining marks, still
round-trips byte for byte. A leading byte order mark is kept as
U+FEFF, as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention UTF-8 in the data file guide
commitResults.messageBody:
A file saved in another encoding is now treated as invalid, so say
so in the UG. Also write the byte order mark in a test as an escape.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix follow-up doc claims and test ordering
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG and DG glossary said a past follow-up date can record a
follow-up that already happened. The app treats any past date as a
pending, overdue follow-up: the card shows it in red with (overdue),
due lists it, and done completes it. Reword both to match.

The DG manual test for adding a contact with a future follow-up date
runs right after the filtered-delete test, which leaves a find filter
active. The new contact is then hidden and the result gets a hidden
contact note, so the expected result fails. Add a prerequisite to run
list first, and say how a past date shows on the card.

The due and delete sequence diagrams both end the parser lifeline at
the destroy marker, so drop the notes claiming a PlantUML limitation
keeps it going.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sort same-day due contacts word by word
commitResults.messageBody:
The due command broke ties between contacts due on the same date with
a root-locale collator. That collator ignores spaces and hyphens, so
"Lim Bo" was listed before "Li Mei" and "Tanaka" before "Tan Wei".

Names are now split into words at spaces and hyphens and compared word
by word, so a shorter word sorts before a longer one it starts with.
Words are compared by base letters first, then accents, then case,
each across the whole name, so accented names still sit next to their
base letter and a capital in one word never outranks a different
letter in a later word. Remaining ties fall back to the whole name and
then the raw text, so the order never depends on insertion order.

isPast() read LocalDate.now() directly, so FollowUpTest built its
dates from the real clock and could fail if it ran across midnight.

Add isPast(Clock) and make the no-arg isPast() delegate to it with
the system clock, so existing callers keep working. The tests now use
fixed clocks at 23:59:59 and 00:00:00 around a date change, across a
year end and in two time zones.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject repeated keys and deep nesting in JSON
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file with the same key twice in one object loaded only the last
value. Two "persons" lists loaded just the second one with no backup,
so the next save deleted the first list for good. A repeated "tags" or
"interactionNotes" key set to null skipped the constructor's null check
and crashed startup with no backup (#216).

Deeply nested junk, e.g. 50,000 levels of "{"a":" before the contact
list, overflowed the stack while Jackson buffered it, so the app
crashed on every launch without making a backup.

Turn on Jackson's strict duplicate detection when reading, and check
the nesting depth in a streaming pass that uses no recursion before
the object mapping runs. Data files are at most five levels deep, so
the limit is 100 levels, well below the depth that overflows even a
256 KB thread stack. Both problems now raise an IOException, so the
data file goes through the usual path: a .bak copy and an empty list.
A preferences file with either problem falls back to the defaults.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split due names at commas and periods too
commitResults.messageBody:
Names may contain commas and periods, but only spaces and hyphens
split words, so "Tan, Ann" was compared as the word "Tan," and sorted
after "Tan Zed", and "J.Tan" was one word sorted after "J. Zed".

Commas and periods now end a word as well, so "Tan, Ann" and
"Tan,Ann" sort as Tan + Ann and "J. Tan" and "J.Tan" as J + Tan.
Apostrophes and slashes still stay inside a word (O'Brien, s/o).

Also correct the collator comment, which said every collator only
sees single words, and explain why the raw text fallback stays: no
two different valid names tie on the collator today, but it keeps
the order total if the name rules ever change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow more marks per letter in tags
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags allowed at most two combining marks on each letter, so common
words such as Hindi "ज़िंदगी" (life) and Burmese "လျှော့" (reduce)
were rejected, even though the user guide says tags accept letters
from any language. The error message also blamed spaces or symbols,
which was wrong for these words.

Let each letter carry up to five marks. Burmese is the script that
needs the most: two medials, a two-part vowel and a tone mark can sit
on one letter. Hindi, Bengali and pointed Hebrew need three, and
Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Thai, Khmer, Arabic and Vietnamese
need two or fewer. Six or more marks on one letter is still rejected,
so piled-up "zalgo" text stays out.

Also reject the Khmer inherent vowels U+17B4 and U+17B5. Unicode marks
them as default ignorable and they draw nothing, so "vip" with one of
them added looked the same as "vip" and a contact could show two
identical tags. Every other default ignorable character was already
rejected; a new test checks the full list.

Update the error message and the user guide tip to mention the mark
limit and invisible characters.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say where a repeated JSON key is
commitResults.messageBody:
Jackson 2.7 reports a repeated key as just "Duplicate field 'name'",
with no line or column, so the key is hard to find in a data file with
thousands of contacts.

Check repeated keys in the same streaming pass that checks the nesting
depth, and report them with the line and column where the repeated key
starts, the same way the depth and trailing content errors do. Jackson's
own check stays on as a fallback.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say that marks count toward the tag length
commitResults.messageBody:
Note in the UG that accents and marks count toward the 50 character
limit, and move the tag examples earlier in the error message so it
reads better.

This branch also edits the data file caution in the user guide and
JsonAddressBookStorageTest, which reject-invalid-utf8-data edits too.
Building on both open branches keeps this one free of conflicts.

commitResults.messageTitle: Point trailing-content errors at the extra text
commitResults.messageBody:
For a // comment or a lone / after the data, Jackson's token location
is still the closing brace of the valid JSON, so the error sent the
user to the wrong place. Its error location is no better, as it lands
past the start of the stray text.

Find the first character after the JSON value that is not a space,
tab or line break, and report its line and column instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refuse a backup that is the data file itself
commitResults.messageBody:
If addressbook.json is a link to addressbook.json.bak, or both are
hard links to one file, Files.copy copies nothing, yet the log said
the backup was made. The app then started empty and the next save
replaced the only copy of the data.

Treat this case as a failed backup, so startup stops and the file is
left as it is. A .bak that is a link to the data file is still fine,
because the copy replaces the link instead of following it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match the data file caution to what is accepted
commitResults.messageBody:
The guide said only spaces or blank lines may follow the final }, but
tabs are accepted too. Say spaces, tabs or line breaks, which is
exactly what the app allows.

Also add a data file that links to its own backup to the list of
things to check when the backup fails.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make the long tag test fail without its guard
commitResults.messageBody:
The test for overly long tag input still passed with the
MAX_INPUT_LENGTH check removed, since a long run of sigma normalizes
in a few milliseconds and is then rejected by the length check. Its
comment also blamed case mapping, which isValidTagName never does.

Add a long run of combining marks in the wrong order, which takes
over ten seconds to normalize without the guard, and say why the
sigma case is still there.

commitResults.messageTitle: Drop the no-op NFC pass in the tag comparison key
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag name passed in is already in NFC, so normalizing it again
did nothing. Replace that pass with an assertion.

The two passes that matter had no test: removing either one kept
every test green, and the test comment that claimed to cover one of
them passed either way. Add a Greek pair that needs the pass after
lowercasing and a dotless i pair that needs the pass after
uppercasing, and fix the old comment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the unused due usage message
commitResults.messageBody:
DueCommand.MESSAGE_USAGE was never read. DueCommandParser gives the
same specific days message for every bad input, which the parser
tests and the DG manual test expect, and the help window and user
guide already explain the command.

Showing the usage text for some inputs instead would change what
users see and make due abc and due 7 days give different errors, so
delete the constant.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add prerequisites to two data file manual tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The corrupted data file test opens data/addressbook.json, but the
missing data file test before it leaves no such file, since showing
the sample contacts does not save them. The older data file test
edits a contact, but the failed backup test before it leaves invalid
data and an empty list.

Say what each test needs and give an add command that sets it up.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say when the overdue marker updates
commitResults.messageBody:
A contact card works out its overdue marker when it is drawn, and a
due list keeps the date it was run with. If the app stays open past
midnight, neither changes by itself, and add, edit or delete on
another contact does not redraw the card either.

Tell users that list, find or due brings them up to date.
Clarify data save error messages

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix a stale Javadoc link and hidden test chars
commitResults.messageBody:
requireValidStructure linked requireNoTrailingContent(JsonParser),
but that method now also takes the JSON text, so the link pointed at
a signature that no longer exists.

JsonUtilTest held a raw no-break space and an ideographic space that
look like ordinary spaces in an editor. Write them as Unicode escapes
like the neighbouring cases so the intent is visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add description line to UG due section
Load data files saved as UTF-8 with a BOM
commitResults.messageBody:
Windows Notepad's "UTF-8 with BOM" and PowerShell 5's
Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 put the bytes EF BB BF before the JSON.
The strictly decoded text then started with U+FEFF, Jackson rejected
it, and the app backed the file up and started with an empty list.
The next command that changed contacts saved only the new contact.

Strip one leading U+FEFF after decoding in FileUtil#readFromFile, so
both the data file and the preferences file accept it. A second mark,
or one later in the file, is still kept as text. Saving never writes
a mark, so such a file is written back without it.

Say in the UG that UTF-8 with or without a byte order mark is fine.

commitResults.messageTitle: List an unreadable data file in the UG checks
commitResults.messageBody:
If addressbook.json cannot be read (no read permission) or is a
folder, startup stops with "Could not back up unreadable data file".
The UG checklist for a failed backup only covered the data folder,
the .bak path and links, so all its checks passed and the user was
left stuck.

Add a check that addressbook.json is a readable file and not a folder.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show list tag filter in the case it was typed
commitResults.messageBody:
`list t/hotLead` said "Listed 2 contacts with tag hotlead." because
PersonMatchesFiltersPredicate kept a lowercased copy of the tag name
just for the message. Matching never used that copy: it goes through
Tag#equals, which already ignores case.

Drop the lowercased copy and have getTagName return the tag's own
spelling, so the message matches what the user typed and what the
cards show. Matching is unchanged.

Update the Javadoc, the tag filter test that expected lowercase, and
the DG manual test results for `list t/REFERRAL`.

commitResults.messageTitle: Count tag marks on the decomposed form
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG and Tag.MESSAGE_CONSTRAINTS say each letter in a tag can carry
up to 5 accents or marks, but marks were counted after NFC. A mark
that NFC folds into a precomposed letter was not counted, so "a" with
6 marks and Vietnamese "ệ" with 5 more marks (7 in all) were accepted
while "x" with 6 marks was rejected.

Match the pattern against the NFD form instead, where every accent is
its own mark, so the documented limit holds however the letter was
typed. The 50 character limit is still counted on the NFC form.

A scan of every code point shows no single character changes answer,
and no precomposed letter carries more than 3 marks, so every real
word in TagTest still passes. Normalizing runs only after the raw and
NFC length checks, so the extra pass is on at most 50 code points.

commitResults.messageTitle: Lighten overdue follow-up red for contrast
commitResults.messageBody:
The "(overdue)" date used #ff8a80, which is only 3.26:1 on odd rows
(#515658) and 3.74:1 on a selected card (#424d5f). WCAG AA asks for
4.5:1 for 13px text.

Use #ffbcb5, the same red hue made lighter. It gives 6.71:1 on even
rows (#3c3e3f), 4.65:1 on odd rows and 5.33:1 on a selected card, so
every row background clears 4.5:1 and the date still reads as red.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document data file loading and due use case
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG did not explain what happens to the data file at startup, so
developers had to read MainApp, JsonUtil, FileUtil and
JsonAddressBookStorage to see when the app loads sample data, starts
empty or refuses to start.

Add an Implementation section with an activity diagram for loading,
checking and backing up the data file, plus design considerations on
starting empty after a backup and on strict parsing.

Add a "Review due follow-ups" use case that matches DueCommand,
including the cases with no contacts due and an invalid DAYS value.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct two design trade-off claims in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The app does not open when the invalid file cannot be backed up, and
unknown fields are dropped on the next save, so say so. Also say the
repeated-key check is about giving the location.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show interaction notes in class diagrams
commitResults.messageBody:
Every Person holds a list of InteractionNote and every
JsonAdaptedPerson saves a list of JsonAdaptedInteractionNote, but the
Model and Storage class diagrams left both out without being marked
as partial.

Add Person *--> "*" InteractionNote to the Model diagram and
JsonAdaptedPerson --> "*" JsonAdaptedInteractionNote to the Storage
diagram. The DG renders these .puml files directly, so there are no
committed images to update.

commitResults.messageTitle: Draw overdue dates at full opacity
commitResults.messageBody:
The theme draws every label at 90% opacity, which brought the overdue
red under 4.5:1 contrast on odd rows (4.10). Draw it at full opacity
so it reaches 6.71, 4.65 and 5.33 on even, odd and selected rows.
Fix singular note count in deletenote error

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for prefs startup, exit and predicates
commitResults.messageBody:
MainApp had no tests for loading a valid preference file, a first
launch with no file, a file that cannot be saved, or saving prefs on
exit. Add tests for each, so a change that stops window settings
being kept between runs is caught.

Also cover FollowUpDueByPredicate#hashCode and #toString, and a Tag
compared with itself.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a tool-use line to the DG acknowledgements
commitResults.messageBody:
Cite the coding assistants Tommy used, as the course asks for
widespread tool use.
Add last contact date

commitResults.messageTitle: Report impossible follow-up dates in data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file with "followUp": "31-02-2026" was rejected with "Follow-up
date must be in DD-MM-YYYY format", although the format is correct.
The add and edit commands already tell these cases apart.

Check the format and the calendar date separately when loading, as
ParserUtil#parseFollowUp does, so an impossible date now reports
"31-02-2026 is not a real date." Last contact dates already use one
message for both cases in the contacted command and in the data file,
so they stay as they are.

The overdue marker on a card is worked out when the card is drawn, so
a follow-up due today was not marked overdue after midnight until a
command such as list rebuilt the cards.

Add MidnightRefresher, which checks the local date just after each
midnight and at least once a minute, and redraws the contact list when
the date changes. The minute check also covers a computer that slept
through midnight. The delay to midnight follows the clock's time zone,
including daylight saving days where midnight is skipped or repeated.

An open due list keeps the cutoff date shown in its result, so the
contacts and index numbers do not change under the user; running due
again moves the cutoff. Update the user guide note to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show why the data file failed to load
commitResults.messageBody:
When the data file is invalid, the app backs it up and opens with an
empty list, but the reason and the backup path only went to the log.
A user who does not read the log thinks the contacts are gone, and the
next change replaces the file.

Keep a startup notice in MainApp when loading fails and show it in the
result box once the window opens. The notice names the data file, the
.bak copy and the reason. Loading errors from the data file now start
with the position of the invalid contact.

commitResults.messageTitle: Narrow the DG claim about loading old data files
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG said data files from older versions still load, but some v1.4
values are rejected by the stricter v1.5 rules, so such a file is
backed up and the app starts with an empty list.

Say only that files without the status and followUp fields still load,
and add a UG known issue that lists the v1.4 values that no longer load
and how to recover them from the .bak copy.

commitResults.messageTitle: Plan optional email and address for add
commitResults.messageBody:
The team has used 9 of its 10 planned enhancement slots. Use the last
one for making e/ and a/ optional in add, since a prospect known only
by name and phone cannot be added without made-up values.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject unpaired surrogate escapes in data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A hand-edited data file could hold half of an emoji pair as a JSON
escape, such as \ud83c. Strict UTF-8 decoding does not catch this, so
the file loaded without a backup, and the next save wrote the text as
"?" for good.

Check every string and field name in JsonUtil.requireValidStructure and
reject a lone surrogate with its line and column, so the normal backup
path runs. Escaped pairs that form a whole character still load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Sort stroke letters by base letter in due
commitResults.messageBody:
The collator treats letters with a stroke, such as Đ, Ł, Ħ and Ø, as
separate letters after Z, so on the same date Đặng and Łukasz were
listed after Zack.

Read these letters as their base letter in the base-letter pass of the
name comparison only. The accent and case passes still see the original
letters, so on a full tie the plain letter comes first and the order
stays total.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report missing n/ when add has text before it
commitResults.messageBody:
Typing the name without n/, as in "add John Doe p/98765432 ...", gave
the general "Invalid command format!" message, although leaving out
other prefixes gives the targeted missing-field message.

When there is text before the first prefix and n/ is absent, report the
missing fields, which then include n/NAME. Text before n/ itself still
gives the general message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say how tag length is counted in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG said accents and marks count toward the 50 characters, but a tag
of 50 copies of é or ệ is accepted, because length is counted after
letters and accents are combined.

State that rule: an accent that merges into its letter does not count
separately, while other marks do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give plain reasons for JSON errors at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
The startup notice passed on Jackson's own messages, which name
internal classes, quote the file and can give a wrong column, e.g. for
a file that stops in the middle of the contact list.

Replace parse errors and wrong-shape data with short plain reasons that
give only the line, and say that a file that ends early is cut off.
Report an empty file as such instead of "No content to map". Our own
messages, such as an invalid contact or a repeated key, are kept.

Show the data and backup paths the same way as the status bar does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap long lines in the result box
commitResults.messageBody:
The result box did not wrap text, so long lines such as the add usage
or a long reason in the startup notice were cut off at the default
window size and needed sideways scrolling. Lines with their own line
breaks look the same as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: List more v1.4 values that no longer load
commitResults.messageBody:
Emails over 254 characters and follow-up dates in the year 0000 were
valid in v1.4 but are rejected now, so a v1.4 file with them is also
backed up and loads as an empty list. Add both to the UG known issue.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep planned enhancement 10 to the add command
commitResults.messageBody:
Drop the sentence about adding or removing an email with edit, so the
enhancement stays one change to add.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract the duplicate key check in JsonUtil
commitResults.messageBody:
requireValidStructure tracked nesting depth and duplicate keys in one
loop, four levels deep, and assumed without saying so that a field
name only appears while an object is open.

Move the duplicate key check into requireUniqueKey, next to
requireNoUnpairedSurrogate, and state that assumption as an assert.
The loop now only tracks depth and calls the two checks. The error
message and the token it reports are unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy loops, limits and timing in TagTest
commitResults.messageBody:
Two equality tests repeated the same pairwise loop with an if inside.
Move it into assertEqualsConsistentWithHashCode, which asserts the same
properties without branching, and check that distinct names give
distinct tags with one set size assertion.

Use Tag.MAX_LENGTH instead of the literals 50 and 51, so the boundary
tests follow the limit if it changes.

Drop the timing loops that repeated 10,000 validations and 2,000,000
comparisons under a two second limit, as they could fail on a slow
machine. Each long name is still checked once under the limit, and
the longest tags with a final sigma are still checked to be equal.

Several storage and JSON tests copied the same helpers that build
files with bad bytes. Move them into TestUtil and reuse them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject other commands' prefixes in find
commitResults.messageBody:
find n/John, find st/CLIENT and find t/referral searched for those
words in names and quietly reported 0 contacts, although John Tan and
three clients exist.

find now names the first app prefix it does not take and says that it
only searches names, or phone numbers with p/, and that list st/STATUS
or list t/TAG filters by status or tag. The name words a/l, a/p and
d/o are still searched as names, and mixing a name with p/ keeps its
current message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say phone separators must be single
commitResults.messageBody:
A phone such as 9123  4567 or 9123 - 4567 was rejected with a message
saying spaces or dashes are allowed between digits, which the input
seems to follow. The hidden rule is that two separators in a row are
not allowed.

The message now says digits may be separated by a single space or
dash and gives an example. The UG phone line says the same.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject note and contact prefixes in add and edit
commitResults.messageBody:
add n/Bob Lim nt/Met at roadshow ... saved the contact as "Bob Lim
nt/Met at roadshow", because add and edit do not know the nt/ and d/
prefixes of the note and contacted commands, so the text stayed in
the field before it.

add and edit now reject any app prefix they do not take, name it and
point to the command that uses it, e.g. "nt/ is not used by add. Use
note INDEX nt/NOTE to add a note." Only the app's own lowercase
prefixes after whitespace count, and d/o is treated as part of a name,
so names such as "Raj s/o Kumar" and "Aisha d/o Rahman" still work.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix find and edit details in the guides
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG find examples were left over from AddressBook, the find format
left out "...", although any number of keywords is accepted, and the
description said names must start with a keyword, while find matches
the start of any word in a name.

The find examples now use the sample contacts, every find format
(UG, DG use case, planned enhancement 9 and help window) ends in
"...", and the description says a word in the name is matched. The UG
edit section and the DG Edit use case now say that renaming a contact
to another contact's name is refused, with the exact message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Back up data file with a control-character address
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file whose address is only control characters, such as
"\u0001", stopped the app at every launch with no window and no .bak.
The raw value passed the storage check, but the Address constructor
trims it to "" and threw an IllegalArgumentException that loading did
not catch.

Loading now treats a value that a model constructor rejects as
invalid data, so the file is copied to .bak and the app starts empty
with the usual message naming the contact.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check the date on a daemon thread, not a timer
commitResults.messageBody:
The midnight check used a JavaFX PauseTransition. While an animation
runs, JavaFX keeps its pulse timer ticking about 60 times a second, so
an idle window used noticeably more CPU than before.

Wait on a single daemon thread from a ScheduledExecutorService instead,
using the same delay (just after midnight, at most a minute), and run
the date check on the JavaFX thread with Platform.runLater. The main
window stops the refresher when it is hidden, which covers both the
exit command and the close button. The scheduler and UI executor can
be passed in, so the scheduling is tested without JavaFX.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match prefix check doc to how it splits words
commitResults.messageBody:
The Javadoc of findUnsupportedPrefix said it finds prefixes as
ArgumentTokenizer does, but it splits words on spaces, tabs and line
breaks while the tokenizer only looks after a plain space. The doc now
says so and why: a prefix typed after a tab is reported instead of
being saved into the field before it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use one style for unsupported prefix errors
commitResults.messageBody:
find said "find does not use st/. ..." while add and edit said "nt/ is
not used by add. ...". find now uses the same form, e.g. "st/ is not
used by find. It only searches names, or phone numbers with p/, ...",
built by one shared ParserUtil method. The UG quote of the message is
updated to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that ALL_PREFIXES lists every prefix
commitResults.messageBody:
add, edit and find reject an app prefix they do not take only if it is
in CliSyntax.ALL_PREFIXES. A new prefix left out of that list would be
saved into fields again, so a test now reads every Prefix constant in
CliSyntax and checks that the list has each of them exactly once.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fold accented stroke letters in due sorting
commitResults.messageBody:
A stroke letter that also carries an accent as one character, such as
the O with stroke and acute, was not in the fold list, so on the same
date "Ǿrn Bo" was listed after Zack instead of next to "Ørn Ann".

Decompose each word before folding stroke letters in the base-letter
pass, so the accent is split off and the letter folds to its base. The
accent and case passes are unchanged.
